description: Run an energy-landscape job (wai.quantum.landscape/1): no circuit, but an energy over variables of three states (+, - and 0, where 0 is left out at its own cost), written in epuML, and a state of low energy found by the settling model's reference kernels, a classical emulator, in software. The answer gives the state, its exact energy, every arrangement checked where the program has at most 16 variables (truth, reached), the program's own checks, a verdict (solved, missed, failed or unchecked) with its reason, the work counted, the joules priced at rates measured elsewhere (never metered: say priced), and a replay digest anyone can reproduce. Sealed with the service's key; verify_quantum_receipt checks it, its form included (quantum-landscape §5.4). Nothing here is a quantum effect. Quote the verdict and the numbers; a program refused is refused with its line.

op.description: run: one run, its state, its energy, every arrangement checked up to 16 variables, the priced joules and the replay digest; sweep: the program at each temperature; compare: the same budget on simulated annealing, tabu search and greedy descent; replay: many seeds, one line each.

parity.description: statistical also takes a kernel graded statistical (default bit-exact).

program.description: The program in epuML, one statement a line: `vars N` first; `agree I J` (+1), `oppose I J` (-1), `couple I J W`, `weight I J W` (real, quantised to its sign), `pin I +|-`, `lean I +|-`, `field I B`, `cost C`; and last the run line, `minimize [steps=S]` (temperature 0) or `solve [t0=T] [restarts=R] [steps=S]`. `#! check different 0-1 1-2`, `#! check permutation M`, `#! check balance A B C`, `#! check matches +-0+` say how to check an answer. A state is one character a variable: + - 0.

seed.description: The seed: a whole number, or a string of up to 20 digits (default 1).

seeds.description: sweep, compare, replay: how many seeds (default 20).

temperature.description: The starting temperature, over the program's own: 0 is the deterministic mode; a decimal string like "0.5" keeps every bit.
